stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist has completed the required administration training and maintains current CPR certification. Each option involves a medication that appears on the MH/SUD administration list. Which requests may proceed under the current guidance? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A 34-year-old patient has a valid patient-specific prescription for a repeat dose of Vivitrol supplied in its single-dose presentation
A 45-year-old patient has a valid patient-specific prescription for Invega Sustenna, but this would be the patient's first dose of the medication
A 39-year-old patient requests Abilify Maintena from anonymous pharmacy floor stock that is not tied to a patient-specific prescribed single dose
A 17-year-old patient has a valid patient-specific prescription for a repeat dose of Invega Sustenna
A 52-year-old patient has a valid patient-specific prescription for a repeat dose of Abilify Maintena supplied as the prescribed single dose

stem: A pharmacy schedules an intern for a shift without a pharmacist preceptor directing the work. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A senior technician may serve as the preceptor.
The intern must work under direct supervision of a registered pharmacist preceptor.
Five hundred internship hours permit independent prescription verification.
Intern status does not authorize independent pharmacist practice.
The pharmacist preceptor remains responsible for the supervision relationship.

stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist completed the appropriate injection-training program and receives a valid patient-specific prescription for a repeat dose of Vivitrol in its single-dose presentation. The prescriber directs pharmacy administration, but the pharmacist's CPR certification expired last week. What is the best action under the current MH/SUD administration guidance?

choices.text: Administer the dose because the medication, prescription, and repeat-dose requirements are otherwise satisfied
Administer the dose after obtaining an additional written patient consent acknowledging that CPR certification has expired
Postpone pharmacist administration until current CPR certification is restored, because current CPR certification is an administrator requirement
Administer the dose if another pharmacy employee with current CPR certification remains in the pharmacy during the injection
Administer the dose if the prescriber gives same-day verbal confirmation that the pharmacist may proceed despite the expired certification

stem:
A Massachusetts retail pharmacy offers medication administration under DCP 26-03-124. The cases do not involve a hospital privilege or a separately authorized opioid treatment program. Each option describes a separate work-queue record. Assume all other prerequisites are satisfied; judge the action and facts actually stated, not an unstated exception.

Which proposed actions are supported by the applicable requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: A pharmacist uses the authority to administer a prescribed HIV-prevention injection as the basis for independently prescribing that injection.
A trained pharmacist with current CPR administers an eligible single-dose LAI to an adult under a valid prescription and product requirements.
A pharmacy administers ceftriaxone intravenously using the circular’s IM authorization.
A pharmacist immediately informs the prescriber after an administration reaction requiring emergency-department monitoring.
A qualified intern administers an eligible adult patient’s IM medication under appropriate pharmacist supervision.

stem:
A Massachusetts retail pharmacy offers medication administration under DCP 26-03-124. The cases do not involve a hospital privilege or a separately authorized opioid treatment program. Each option describes a separate work-queue record. Assume all other prerequisites are satisfied; judge the action and facts actually stated, not an unstated exception.

Which proposed actions are supported by the applicable requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: A trained pharmacist with current CPR administers an eligible single-dose LAI to an adult under a valid prescription and product requirements.
A qualified intern administers an eligible adult patient’s IM medication under appropriate pharmacist supervision.
A pharmacist immediately informs the prescriber after an administration reaction requiring emergency-department monitoring.
A pharmacy documents patient consent, screening, lot, expiry, administration route/site, and administering professional.
A pharmacy administers ceftriaxone intravenously using the circular’s IM authorization.

stem:
A Massachusetts retail pharmacy offers medication administration under DCP 26-03-124. The cases do not involve a hospital privilege or a separately authorized opioid treatment program. Each option describes a separate work-queue record. Assume all other prerequisites are satisfied; judge the action and facts actually stated, not an unstated exception.

Which proposed actions are supported by the applicable requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: A pharmacy documents patient consent, screening, lot, expiry, administration route/site, and administering professional.
A qualified intern administers an eligible adult patient’s IM medication under appropriate pharmacist supervision.
A pharmacist waits for the next routine progress report after an administration reaction requiring emergency-department monitoring.
A trained pharmacist uses the circular to administer the same LAI to a 16-year-old without another lawful authority.
A pharmacist follows labeling and applicable REMS for an eligible long-acting buprenorphine injection.

stem:
A technician qualified to vaccinate is assigned to administer a long-acting injectable antipsychotic under the general medication-administration circular.
A pharmacist proposes using that circular to administer an otherwise eligible medication intravenously to a 17-year-old.

choices.text: Vaccination qualification does not place the technician within this pharmacist-or-intern medication pathway.
A qualified vaccinating technician is automatically included in the general medication-administration circular.
The proposed intravenous administration to a 17-year-old does not meet this pathway's age and route conditions.
The circular permits intravenous administration to a 17-year-old whenever the drug is listed.
An eligible medication must also meet the specified single-dose packaging and prescription conditions.
Being named in the circular alone removes the single-dose packaging and prescription conditions.
The limited individual MCSR exception for administration does not waive all pharmacy facility registrations.
The individual administration exception eliminates the pharmacy's separate registration obligations.

stem:
A pharmacist rejects a valid eligible prescription solely because it lacks the recommended words 'for pharmacist administration.'
A colleague treats the circular's example of quarterly prescriber reassessment as a mandatory new-prescription requirement exactly every 90 days for every product.

choices.text: The absent recommended notation alone is not an automatic invalidity rule stated in the circular.
The circular makes the recommended notation an absolute validity condition for every prescription.
The reassessment example is not a universal exact 90-day new-prescription rule.
The word 'quarterly' creates an exact 90-day new-prescription mandate for all eligible drugs.
A clinically meaningful uncertainty about intended administration should be clarified appropriately.
Because the notation is recommended, actual uncertainty about administration intent may be ignored.
Counseling is provided before administration and is not replaced by a consent signature.
Signing a consent form replaces the circular's pre-administration counseling.

stem:
A Massachusetts pharmacy technician trainee finishes an injection course and is assigned to vaccinate while the pharmacist manages prescriptions nearby.
A fully licensed technician meets the separate vaccination qualifications but proposes vaccinating without approval from the pharmacist on duty.

choices.text: Completing an injection course does not make a technician trainee eligible under the state vaccination policy.
An injection course makes a licensed technician trainee eligible to vaccinate under the state policy.
An eligible technician still needs the on-duty pharmacist's approval and direct supervision by a qualified immunizing pharmacist.
A qualified technician's training certificate replaces on-duty approval and direct pharmacist supervision.
The pharmacist retains vaccine selection and counseling duties before technician administration.
A technician's permission to inject includes independent vaccine selection and patient counseling.
The intern pathway also requires the specified supervision rather than independent practice.
An intern's vaccination training creates an independent pharmacist practice privilege.

stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist administers a patient-specific dose of Abilify Maintena under the mental-illness administration pathway. Shortly afterward, the patient develops a severe reaction requiring emergency medical services and evaluation in an emergency department. Which follow-through actions are consistent with current Massachusetts guidance? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Immediately report the adverse event to the prescriber because emergency-department treatment is one of the specified serious outcomes
Record the adverse outcome or adverse event in the pharmacy's administration record
If the event is a dispensing error or a serious adverse drug event, fulfill the pharmacist's or intern's applicable Board reporting responsibility
Delay prescriber communication until the next routine reassessment because the patient has already been transferred to emergency care
Omit the event from the pharmacy record when emergency medical services create their own clinical documentation

stem: A pharmacist discovers that an improper warfarin dispensing caused a patient to be hospitalized, and the facts meet the serious-injury reporting criteria in 247 CMR 20.02(1). Which statements correctly distinguish the duties triggered by this same event? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: The pharmacist’s initial QRE documentation remains subject to the 24-hour discovery-or-notification clock.
The seven-business-day Board reporting period is measured from the date the prescription was originally written.
The manager of record must report the qualifying improper dispensing within seven business days of discovery of the related serious injury or death.
Completing the QRE record eliminates the separate serious-event report because both rules concern the same dispensing error.
The event can trigger both CQI documentation and the separate serious-event reporting pathway because the rules have different purposes and clocks.

stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist administers an eligible patient-specific long-acting antipsychotic under the current MH/SUD pathway. Which workflow principles are consistent with the guidance? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Send the administration record to the prescriber as soon after administration as practical, as strongly encouraged by DCP guidance
Allow a cashier to perform the injection after the pharmacist verifies the prescription
Skip privacy protections because the medication treats mental illness
Use a prescribed single dose supplied in eligible single-dose packaging
Document the administration in the pharmacy's patient record

stem:
The pharmacy is using the non-vaccine medication-administration pathway in DCP 26-03-124. Personnel, patient, product, and prescription requirements are otherwise met. An administration-related reaction causes a persistent significant incapacity.

Which response accurately reflects the circular’s wording? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Immediately report the event to the prescriber; assess any separate Board reporting duties.
Appropriately communicate the reaction to the prescriber within 24 hours as the circular recommends.
Follow the prescriber’s appropriate reassessment interval; quarterly is an example rather than a universal fixed deadline.
Use professional judgment and contact the prescriber as encouraged to clarify the intended administration setting.

stem:
After an eligible medication injection, the patient requires additional treatment and monitoring in an emergency department; staff plan to wait 24 hours before notifying the prescriber.
A nonserious reaction in another patient is discussed under the circular's recommendation for communication within 24 hours.

choices.text: The serious outcome requires immediate prescriber notification rather than waiting for the routine interval.
The pharmacy may delay the serious-outcome notification for the full 24-hour routine interval.
The ordinary 24-hour communication wording is a recommendation distinct from the immediate mandatory category.
The circular uses the same mandatory 24-hour deadline for serious and nonserious reactions.
Emergency care must not be delayed while staff finish the report.
Completing the report takes priority over necessary emergency care.
A prescriber call does not replace a separately triggered Board report for an error or serious event.
Calling the prescriber completes every otherwise applicable Board reporting duty.

stem:
Improper dispensing leads to an emergency-department visit with additional treatment and monitoring, but the patient is not admitted as an inpatient.
A manager classifies the event as nonserious solely because it did not cause death or inpatient admission.

choices.text: The additional emergency-department treatment and monitoring may satisfy the described serious-injury definition.
Absence of inpatient admission excludes the event from the described serious-injury definition.
The manager must apply the actual definition rather than use death or admission as the exclusive test.
Death or inpatient admission are the exclusive criteria in the described Massachusetts definition.
A state SADE definition and the federal 503B serious-and-unexpected standard are separate frameworks.
The Massachusetts SADE definition is interchangeable with the federal 503B serious-and-unexpected standard.
Subsequent clinical information may change which reporting triggers the pharmacy must assess.
The first clinical description fixes the reporting assessment even if more serious outcomes later appear.

stem:
An event after vaccination falls within the applicable VAERS reportable-events table and time interval, but causation has not been proven.
The pharmacy enters the vaccination into MIIS and believes this also completes adverse-event reporting.

choices.text: Lack of proven causation does not by itself eliminate the specified VAERS report.
VAERS reporting must wait until the pharmacy proves the vaccine caused the event.
Recording the dose in MIIS does not substitute for the applicable VAERS report.
A completed MIIS dose record is also the required VAERS adverse-event report.
An event identified by the manufacturer as a contraindication to further doses is a policy reporting category.
A manufacturer-identified contraindication to further doses is excluded from the policy's reporting categories.
Immediate patient care and any independently triggered Board reporting remain separate tasks.
Submitting VAERS removes the need for immediate care and any otherwise required Board report.

stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist has completed no training programme of any kind. She proposes to dispense emergency contraception under the statewide standing order this week, and to dispense a COVID-19 drug under a standing order next week. How do the two proposals compare?

choices.text: The emergency contraception dispensing may proceed; the COVID-19 drug may not.
The COVID-19 dispensing may proceed; the emergency contraception may not.
Both may proceed, because training is a professional expectation rather than a bar.
Neither may proceed, because both regimes require approved training beforehand.
Both may proceed once she notifies the Department that she intends to dispense.

stem: A prescriber's office telephones a Massachusetts pharmacy with a new prescription while the pharmacist on duty is counselling another patient. Which statements about who may take the call are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Only the pharmacist may take a new prescription by telephone.
Any pharmacy employee may take it and pass it to the pharmacist to check.
A pharmacy intern may receive a new prescription over the telephone.
An uncertified technician may take it provided the pharmacist verifies it afterwards.
A certified technician with the on-duty pharmacist's approval may receive it.

stem: An adult asks a trained Massachusetts pharmacist to prescribe a self-administered oral hormonal contraceptive. She has never previously received a contraceptive prescription. What is the most accurate response under the pharmacist-prescribing statute?

choices.text: A prior prescription is mandatory before a pharmacist may use this pathway.
Lack of a prior prescription is not itself a bar; the pharmacist still must follow the required screening and protocol process.
The pharmacist may prescribe any contraceptive dosage form because the patient has no prior prescription.
The patient must first obtain a controlled-substance registration because hormonal contraception is Schedule II.
The pharmacist may skip the self-screening risk assessment when the patient is a first-time user.

stem:
Case A: A pharmacist chooses the statewide emergency-contraception standing-order pathway but assumes an additional training course is a mandatory entry condition under that pathway.

Case B: An agent requests a standing-order prescription for someone who will take the medication, but the pharmacist has not contacted or assessed that person.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case B? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The described statewide EC pathway requires the assumed additional course before any participation.
Using the EC standing order authorizes independent prescribing of unrelated products.
The actual intended user must be assessed through the allowed in-person or telephone pathway.
Voluntary participation eliminates every separate duty to provide access to valid prescriptions.

stem:
Case A: A pharmacist chooses the statewide emergency-contraception standing-order pathway but assumes an additional training course is a mandatory entry condition under that pathway.

Case B: An agent requests a standing-order prescription for someone who will take the medication, but the pharmacist has not contacted or assessed that person.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: Participation in this service is voluntary, while independently applicable dispensing-access duties remain.
The described statewide EC pathway does not impose the additional mandatory training assumed in the first case.
The standing order is a specific authority rather than a general independent prescribing license.
The actual intended user must be assessed through the allowed in-person or telephone pathway.

The agent's request alone replaces assessment of the actual intended user for a standing-order prescription.

stem:
A pharmacist dispenses naloxone under a statewide standing order and assumes that this creates the same authority as an individualized CDTM agreement.
A pharmacy sells an approved OTC contraceptive and interprets that sale as evidence that every pharmacist may independently prescribe all contraceptive formulations.

choices.text: A standing-order dispensing pathway is distinct from patient-specific CDTM authority.
Dispensing under a statewide standing order automatically creates a CDTM agreement.
An OTC product's purchase pathway does not define a pharmacist's independent prescribing scope.
OTC sale of one contraceptive authorizes independent prescribing of all contraceptive formulations.
Medication administration is a separate act from prescribing or dispensing.
Permission to prescribe a product automatically grants permission to administer it by any route.
A CDTM arrangement needs the specified individual, setting, agreement, and patient authorization.
A pharmacy's facility license by itself supplies all CDTM authority.

stem:
A minor seeks emergency contraception through the described Massachusetts pathway, and staff add a blanket parental-consent requirement.
The pharmacy reports its EC services using a naloxone-specific deadline without identifying any EC authority establishing that deadline.

choices.text: The described EC access guidance does not require parental consent for the minor's EC access.
The pharmacy may present parental consent as a universal legal prerequisite for this EC pathway.
The naloxone deadline should not be attributed to EC reporting without an EC source.
An annual reporting requirement makes the naloxone deadline applicable to EC automatically.
Standing-order dispensing connects to a patient-specific prescription, labeling, and records.
A standing order eliminates the need to create the required patient-specific dispensing record.
The EC consent rule does not establish unrestricted minor consent for every other health service.
A minor's EC access creates unrestricted consent authority for every unrelated treatment.
